{{nihongo|'''Sasamuta Shrine'''|西寒多神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bungo Province]].

=== History ===
[[File:Hongusan.JPG|thumb|right|Motomiyayama]]

=== Founding ===
According to ``Oita Gunshi,'' {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} visited Mt. Nishikanta (currently {{ill|Mount Hongū|Q11520121|qid=Q11520121|lt=Mt. Hongu}}) on her way back from {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}} and planted a white flag on the mountaintop as proof of her visit. The local people revered it and tied a fence around it to worship it. Later, in April 1999, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} built a shrine on Mt. Hongu, which is said to be the founding shrine. </ref>.

From this tradition, it is believed that Mt. Hongu was established as {{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}}. </ref><ref name="place name"/>.

=== Outline ===
The first look at {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi}} is from ``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'' {{ill|Jōgan|de|Jōgan|es|Jōgan|fa|جوگان|fr|Ère Jōgan|ia|Jogan|id|Jōgan|ja|貞観 (日本)|ko|조간 (연호)|ru|Дзёган|simple|Jōgan|sr|Џоган|tr|Jōgan|uk|Дзьоґан (ненґо)|zh|貞觀 (日本)|zh_yue|貞觀 (日本)|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}}11 ({{ill|869|Q23917|qid=Q23917}}) This is an article dated March 22, which states that Nishikanta-jin is bestowed with the rank of Junior Fifth Rank and Lower. In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, it is described as ``Nishikata Shrine'' in {{ill|Bungo Province|Q864148|qid=Q864148}}{{ill|Ōita District, Ōita|Q8081521|qid=Q8081521}}, making it the only major shrine in Bungo Province. It is also said to have been revered as Bungo Province {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. Although it declined after the late {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, it was revered by the feudal lord {{ill|Ōtomo clan|Q1096662|qid=Q1096662}} from the medieval period onwards.

May 14th, {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}4 ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was ranked as {{ill|Kokuhei Chūsha|qid=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha}}, and after World War II, it became {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

=== Historical evidence ===

==== Formula internal ratio ====
Another non-sha of Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine, Oita District, Bungo Province'' is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishikata Shrine}} (Usuki City, Oita Prefecture). In "Bungo no Kunishi" and "Dazai Kannaishi", it is said that this is the main shrine, and it is said that {{ill|Ōtomo Chikayo|Q11433259|qid=Q11433259}} was moved to the current location in March 15th year ({{ill|1408|Q6138|qid=Q6138}}).<ref name="place name"/> On the other hand, there is a strong opinion that this is the main shrine due to the area of ​​Oita County and the folklore of Mt. Hongu <ref name="Kami"/>.

==== Specification of Ichinomiya, Bungo Province ====
Our comparison to Ichinomiya is based on <ref name="Gods"/> such as "Bungo kokushi", "Dazai Kannaishi", "Oita gunshi", etc. On the other hand, Ichinomiya in Bungo Province also claims {{ill|Yusuhara Hachimangū|Q195715|qid=Q195715}}. There is a historical document from the year 3 ({{ill|Kaō (era)|Q1150842|qid=Q1150842}} ({{ill|1171|Q19685|qid=Q19685}}) that refers to "Yuhara Hachimangu Shrine" as Ichinomiya. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangu Shrine}}There is a strong view that the separate shrine, Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, was converted into an Ichinomiya Shrine instead of our company. 48. </ref>{{Sfn|Uninomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=598}}. Although the basis for writing about Ichinomiya is unknown, the ``Shokoku Ichinomiya Jinmyo Cho'' (established before 1375) mentions Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, and the ``{{ill|Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|Q11435648|qid=Q11435648}}'' (established around the 16th century) mentions our company <ref> ``Historical Development of the Medieval Ichinomiya System Volume 2'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 367. </ref>.

In connection with this, the {{ill|Pratītyasamutpāda|Q522046|qid=Q522046}} of the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga}} ({{ill|1781|Q7719|qid=Q7719}}) includes a tradition that ``Our company is also called Yusuhara Shrine'' and considers the two shrines to be the same <ref name="place name"/>. However, this is seen as a mistake<ref name="Gods"/>.

=== Precincts ===

=== Shrine building ===
The shrine that stands to the right of the main shrine was built in 1886. {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025|lt=Irimoya}}'s {{ill|Azekura-zukuri|Q2875112|qid=Q2875112|lt=Irimoya-zukuri}}. It has been designated as a cultural property of Oita City.

* Katsuya (arch height): 3.9 meters
* Completion: Bunkyu 2 (1862)* Stonemason: Gobei Goto (2nd generation)
* Cultural property designation, etc.: Oita Prefecture designated tangible cultural property

=== Main festivals ===

=== Shikinen Festival ===
* '''Okamiso Festival'' (Kanmiso Festival)
*: Special ritual. It is held on the day of the annual festival every 33rd year. The ceremony, which is the annual grand festival in which the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine clothing}} of the enshrined deity is newly made and presented, is based on the history book. </ref>.
* '''Shinko Taisai'''' (Goshinko Festival)
*: Held every third year.

=== Annual festival ===
*Monthly festival (1st day of every month)
* New Year's Day Festival (January 1st)
* Harvest Star Festival (February 1st-3rd)
* Prayer Festival (March 15th)
* Hongu Spring Festival (March 20th)
* Annual festival (April 15th)
* Fuji Festival (May 3rd-5th)
*: The {{ill|Wisteria floribunda|ar|وستارية كثيرة الأزهار|arz|وستاريه كثيرة الازهار|ceb|Wisteria floribunda|cs|Vistárie květnatá|de|Japanische Wisteria|es|Wisteria floribunda|eu|Japoniako glizina|fi|Japaninsinisade|fr|Wisteria floribunda|it|Wisteria floribunda|ja|フジ (植物)|ko|등 (식물)|pl|Glicynia japońska|sv|Wisteria floribunda|th|วีสเตียเรียญี่ปุ่น|uk|Ґліцинія японська|uz|Wisteria floribunda|vi|Wisteria floribunda|war|Wisteria floribunda|zh|多花紫藤|qid=Q1329209|lt=Fuji}} flowers near Mannen Bridge are at their peak. Temple festivals, tree growing festivals, memorial services, water god festivals, and Kangaku festivals are held.
* Great Purification (June 30th)
* Summer festival (last Sunday of July)
* Hongu Autumn Festival (October 20th)
* Niinamesai (November 23rd)
* Great Purification, New Year's Eve Festival, Komori Fuda Burning Festival (December 31st)

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Cultural property designated by Oita Prefecture ===
* Mannenbashi Bridge (Tangible Cultural Property) - Designated on April 8, 1982.

=== Cultural property designated by Oita City ===
[[File:Sasamuta-jinja Fuji.JPG|thumb|right|Yama Fuji (city natural monument)]]
* Jinko (tangible cultural property) - Designated on January 9, 1972.
* {{ill|Wisteria brachybotrys|ar|وستارية قصيرة العناقيد|ceb|Wisteria brachybotrys|fr|Wisteria brachybotrys|it|Wisteria brachybotrys|ja|ヤマフジ|sv|Wisteria brachybotrys|vi|Wisteria brachybotrys|war|Wisteria brachybotrys|qid=Q5783537}} (natural monument) - Over 450 years old, tree height 3.5m, trunk circumference 2.8m<ref>[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1219359740812/index.html List of Oita City designated famous trees (tree section)] Oita City</ref><ref>[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1166682381846/index.html Oita City designated famous trees No. 12, 13, 14] Oita City Children's Page</ref>. Designated on January 9, 1972 <ref>[http://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1275373722750/index.html List of cultural properties designated by country, prefecture, and city] Oita City</ref>. It is also designated as a famous tree designated by Oita City (tree category).

=== Others ===

({{Wiki coordinates|33|10|34.00|N|131|35|46.04|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|location|name=Reference: Nearest bus stop "Fujigaoka Minami"}}, about 8 minutes walk after getting off)
